approach: Write Newton's second law for each of the three blocks along its direction of motion, using the same acceleration magnitude for all three since they are connected by inextensible strings.

steps.text: Block A (4 kg) is pulled toward the pulley by tension T₁ and opposed by friction, since its surface has μ = 0.2.
steps.equation: T₁ − μ m_A g = m_A a  →  T₁ − 0.2×4×10 = 4a  →  T₁ = 8 + 4a

steps.text: Block B (8 kg) is pulled toward the pulley by tension T₂ on a frictionless surface.
Block C (20 kg) hangs and is pulled down by gravity and held up by both string tensions.
steps.equation: m_C g − T₁ − T₂ = m_C a  →  200 − T₁ − T₂ = 20a

steps.text: Substitute T₁ and T₂ from the first two equations into the third and solve for a.
steps.why_this_step: Combining all three equations removes the tensions and leaves one equation in the single unknown a.

steps.text: Substitute a = 6 m/s² back to get the tensions.

final_answer.value: a = 6 m/s², T₁ = 32 N, T₂ = 48 N

common_mistakes.text: Forgetting the friction term for block A and writing T₁ = m_A a gives T₁ = 24 N instead of 32 N, changing every later step.
Adding friction on block B even though its surface is frictionless gives a wrong, smaller acceleration.
